variations.name: HEFA sustainable aviation fuel
variations.description: Hydrotreats waste fats, used cooking oil, and vegetable oils into drop-in jet fuel; it supplies ~80% of all SAF today and is the only pathway producing at large commercial scale, making it the workhorse of near-term aviation decarbonization despite a hard ceiling on waste-lipid feedstock.

companies.name: Neste
companies.what: World's largest SAF producer; converted refineries in Singapore and Rotterdam dedicate ~1.5 Mt/yr to SAF capability
companies.signal: Rotterdam SAF line (500 kt/yr) started April 2025, bringing global SAF capability to 1.5 Mt/yr; long-term offtakes with Lufthansa, United, Air France-KLM

companies.name: World Energy
companies.what: First commercial SAF supplier (Paramount, CA since 2016); converting its Houston biorefinery into a 250M gal/yr SAF hub
companies.signal: DOE invited Part II application for ~$2B loan guarantee (2024); 70M-gallon SAF supply pact with Montana Renewables (2025)

companies.name: Montana Renewables (Calumet)
companies.what: Great Falls, MT refinery conversion; one of North America's largest SAF producers, expanding via the MaxSAF project to ~300M gal/yr
companies.signal: Closed $1.44B DOE loan facility Jan 2025 ($1.67B program); first $782M tranche drawn in 2025 despite federal funding freeze delay

companies.name: EcoCeres
companies.what: Hong Kong-based waste-feedstock biorefiner (used cooking oil) with HEFA plants in Zhangjiagang, China and Pasir Gudang, Malaysia
companies.signal: Malaysia plant (420 kt/yr HVO/SAF/naphtha) commissioned Oct 2025, inaugurated Jan 2026; ~770 kt/yr combined renewable fuels capacity; Bain Capital-backed

companies.name: Diamond Green Diesel (Valero/Darling)
companies.what: Largest US renewable diesel maker; added a 235M gal/yr SAF upgrade at Port Arthur, TX — the biggest single US SAF capacity
companies.signal: Port Arthur SAF unit online since late 2024; part of ~1.2B gal/yr renewable fuels JV

companies.name: Phillips 66
companies.what: Converted its Rodeo, CA oil refinery to one of the world's largest renewable fuels plants with SAF output
companies.signal: Rodeo Renewed (~50,000 bpd renewable fuels) ramped 2024-25 with SAF trains; supplying California airports

companies.name: TotalEnergies
companies.what: Converted French refineries (Grandpuits, Normandy) to co-process and produce HEFA SAF for the EU mandate market
companies.signal: Among top-3 global SAF suppliers by offtake volume; long-term airline contracts through 2030

variations.name: Alcohol-to-jet SAF
variations.description: Chemically dehydrates and oligomerizes ethanol or isobutanol into jet fuel, unlocking the huge existing ethanol industry (and future CO2- or biogas-derived alcohols) as SAF feedstock far beyond the limited supply of waste fats.

companies.name: LanzaJet
companies.what: Built and operates the world's first commercial-scale ethanol-to-jet plant (Freedom Pines Fuels, Soperton, GA — 10M gal/yr) and licenses its ATJ process globally
companies.signal: First commercial-scale ethanol-based jet fuel produced Nov 2025; backers include Suncor, Mitsui, Shell, Airbus, Microsoft Climate Fund; license projects in UK, Japan, Uzbekistan

companies.name: Gevo
companies.what: Isobutanol/ethanol-to-jet developer; Net-Zero 1 (Lake Preston, SD) designed for ~60M gal/yr SAF with on-site CCS
companies.signal: $1.46B DOE loan commitment (Oct 2024); acquired Red Trail Energy ethanol+CCS plant; NZ1 FID still pending — economics strained by denied Summit CO2 pipeline permits

companies.name: Swedish Biofuels
companies.what: Proprietary ATJ-SKA process making fully synthetic (100% drop-in) jet fuel from C2-C5 alcohols, biogas, or CO2+H2
companies.signal: 20,000 t/yr demonstration plant at Brista, Sweden — basic engineering complete, EPCM selected, commissioning targeted mid-2020s

companies.name: Summit Next Gen
companies.what: Developing a large Houston-area ethanol-to-SAF conversion plant using licensed technology, fed by Midwest ethanol
companies.signal: Part of Summit Agricultural Group; planned ~250M gal/yr facility, among the largest announced US ATJ projects

companies.name: Honeywell UOP
companies.what: Licenses ethanol-to-jet process technology (plus the dominant HEFA Ecofining process), letting refiners and developers buy rather than invent ATJ chemistry
companies.signal: ETJ technology selected by multiple announced US ATJ projects

variations.name: Gasification & Fischer-Tropsch SAF from waste/biomass
variations.description: Gasifies municipal solid waste or woody biomass into syngas and synthesizes Fischer-Tropsch jet fuel — promising effectively unlimited cheap feedstock, but historically plagued by feedstock-handling failures, syngas cleanup problems, and capex blowouts.

companies.name: Fulcrum BioEnergy
companies.what: Built the world's first municipal-waste-to-fuels plant (Sierra, NV) feeding FT synthesis
companies.signal: Chapter 11 in September 2024 after ~$1B raised from airlines and oil majors; Sierra plant disabled by nitric acid corrosion and feedstock sludge buildup

companies.name: Red Rock Biofuels
companies.what: Attempted a woody-biomass gasification + FT SAF plant in Lakeview, Oregon
companies.signal: Construction stalled ~2022 after cost overruns; unfinished plant sold at auction — a second high-profile gasification-FT failure alongside Fulcrum

companies.name: DG Fuels
companies.what: Developing a ~$4-5B cellulosic (bagasse/wood waste) FT SAF plant in St. James Parish, Louisiana (~180M gal/yr), one of the largest announced SAF projects
companies.signal: Strategic investment from Airbus; offtakes with Delta and Air France-KLM; FID targeted mid-2020s

companies.name: Velocys
companies.what: Supplies microchannel Fischer-Tropsch reactors that make small-scale FT economic; technology behind the UK Altalto waste-to-SAF project
companies.signal: Taken private in 2024 in a ~$40M rescue (Carbon Direct, Lightrock, GenZero, Kibo); UK government SAF funding supports its black-bag-waste project

companies.name: Aether Fuels
companies.what: Temasek/Xora-incubated startup with 'Aether Aurora' flexible syngas-to-liquids platform tolerant of mixed waste-carbon feedstocks
companies.signal: Venture-stage (~$35M+ raised); pilot-scale technology development in Singapore and US

companies.name: Enerkem
companies.what: Canadian MSW gasification company (Edmonton pioneer plant; Varennes Carbon Recycling project in Québec) producing methanol/ethanol convertible toward jet
companies.signal: Edmonton plant closed and major restructuring 2024-25; Varennes project continuing with government backing

companies.name: Johnson Matthey (with bp)
companies.what: Co-developed FT CANS fixed-bed Fischer-Tropsch technology licensed to waste-to-SAF developers (was selected by Fulcrum, DG Fuels, Strategic Biofuels)
companies.signal: Established catalysis incumbent monetizing SAF via licensing rather than project risk

variations.white_space: Two flagship failures (Fulcrum 2024, Red Rock ~2022) prove the chokepoint is feedstock prep and syngas cleanup at scale, not FT chemistry — yet waste feedstock remains the largest untapped SAF resource; the opening is for modular FT (Velocys/Ineratec-style) paired with already-proven gasifiers or with clean point-source syngas, and for developers who de-risk the front end before scaling.

variations.name: Power-to-liquid e-SAF
variations.description: Synthesizes jet fuel from green hydrogen and captured CO2 (via Fischer-Tropsch, methanol, or direct CO2 electrolysis routes); feedstock is effectively unlimited and lifecycle carbon lowest of any pathway, but cost hinges on cheap clean electricity — EU/UK e-SAF sub-mandates from 2030 create guaranteed demand.

companies.name: Infinium
companies.what: Operates Project Roadrunner in West Texas — the world's first commercial-scale eFuels facility — with the larger SAF-focused Project Pegasus next
companies.signal: Up to ~$1.1B framework from Brookfield (part of $1.7B raised by Infinium+Twelve); offtakes with IAG, American Express GBT

companies.name: Twelve
companies.what: CO2 electrolysis (polymer-electrolyte CO2-to-CO) feeding its E-Jet fuel; AirPlant One in Moses Lake, WA is its first commercial facility
companies.signal: $645M raised (TPG Rise Climate-led project equity + Series C); AirPlant One production from ~2025; offtakes with Alaska Airlines and IAG

companies.name: Ineratec
companies.what: German maker of modular Fischer-Tropsch reactors; building Europe's largest e-fuel plant (ERA ONE, Frankfurt)
companies.signal: €70M EIB venture debt + Breakthrough Energy Catalyst grant (Mar 2025) on top of ~$129M Series B; ERA ONE commissioning mid-2020s

companies.name: Synhelion
companies.what: Solar-thermochemical route: concentrated sunlight drives thermochemical syngas production, cutting dependence on electrolysis
companies.signal: DAWN (Jülich, Germany) — world's first industrial solar fuel plant (2024); SWISS/Lufthansa partnership; RISE commercial plant planned in Spain

companies.name: Air Company
companies.what: CO2-to-alcohols-to-jet (AIRMADE) using proprietary catalysts, originally proven on consumer products (vodka/fragrance)
companies.signal: US DoD contracts (incl. up to ~$65M military SAF deal); JetBlue offtake; venture-backed

companies.name: Norsk e-Fuel
companies.what: Building one of Europe's first industrial PtL e-SAF plants in Mosjøen, Norway, using Sunfire electrolysis and Climeworks DAC within a hydropower grid
companies.signal: Boeing investment (2025); first plant targeting production late 2020s

companies.name: Arcadia eFuels
companies.what: Danish developer of the ENDOR e-SAF plant in Vordingborg — one of the only European e-SAF projects with completed FEED
companies.signal: FEED complete but FID repeatedly delayed awaiting offtakes and financing — emblematic of Europe's e-SAF FID gap

companies.name: OXCCU
companies.what: Oxford spin-out with a one-step CO2+H2-to-jet catalyst that skips the separate FT/upgrading steps, cutting capex
companies.signal: $28M Series B (Sept 2025) with IAG, Safran, Orlen VC; first SAF company to win an ATI Non-CO2 grant; pilot plant at Oxford Airport

companies.name: Metafuels
companies.what: Swiss developer of 'aerobrew' methanol-to-jet technology offering high selectivity to jet from green methanol
companies.signal: $24M Series A (Energy Impact Partners et al.); demo unit with RWE in Germany

variations.name: Emerging SAF routes: pyrolysis, HTL, algae, CO2-to-ethanol chains
variations.description: Earlier-stage chemistry — fast-pyrolysis oil upgrading, hydrothermal liquefaction of wet wastes like sewage biosolids, engineered algae oils, and waste-gas fermentation to ethanol — aimed at unlocking cheap, abundant feedstocks the mainstream pathways cannot use.

companies.name: LanzaTech
companies.what: Gas fermentation converting industrial waste gases and CO2 into ethanol that feeds LanzaJet's ATJ plants — the front half of the CO2-to-jet chain
companies.signal: NASDAQ-listed but distressed: going-concern doubt despite $40M preferred equity (May 2025), 1-for-100 reverse split (Aug 2025) for Nasdaq compliance; licensing deals continue (e.g., Uzbekistan ethanol+SAF complex)

companies.name: Firefly Green Fuels
companies.what: Hydrothermal liquefaction of sewage biosolids into SAF — a negative-cost, city-scale feedstock nobody else uses
companies.signal: Wizz Air offtake; Synagro partnership for North American biosolids; Builders Vision backing; first UK plant targeted 2028/29

companies.name: Alder Renewables
companies.what: Upgrades biomass pyrolysis oil into 'Alder SAF100', a 100% drop-in fuel candidate from woody residues
companies.signal: Backed by United Airlines Ventures, Boeing and Avfuel; pilot-scale production and SAF100 testing underway

companies.name: Viridos
companies.what: Engineered high-lipid algae strains for algal jet fuel (the former ExxonMobil algae program)
companies.signal: ExxonMobil exited 2023 calling algae 'too difficult and expensive'; Chapter 11 April 2025; assets sold to Breakthrough Energy Ventures in a 64-day sale completed Nov 2025

companies.name: Honeywell UOP
companies.what: Offers upgrading technology (e.g., pyrolysis-oil and eFining routes) that lets emerging-feedstock developers reach ASTM-qualified jet
companies.signal: Technology licensed across multiple DOE-supported emerging SAF projects

variations.white_space: Algae has now failed twice at corporate scale (Exxon exit 2023, Viridos Chapter 11 2025) — biology plus harvesting economics remain unsolved physics-of-cost; meanwhile wet-waste HTL has gate-fee-negative feedstock at every city wastewater plant and essentially one credible player (Firefly), so process developers that partner with water utilities face an almost empty field.

variations.name: Battery-electric fixed-wing aircraft
variations.description: Replaces turbines with battery packs and electric motors for true zero-emission flight; today's cell energy density caps useful range at roughly 100-400nm, so the market is flight training, cargo feeders, and 9-90 seat regional designs that bet on future batteries.

companies.name: BETA Technologies
companies.what: ALIA CX300 fixed-wing electric (plus A250 eVTOL) with a build-the-charging-network strategy along the US East Coast
companies.signal: IPO'd on NYSE Oct-Nov 2025 (sought ~$825M at up to $7.2B valuation); $300M GE Aerospace investment; customers include UPS, Bristow, Air New Zealand

companies.name: Eviation
companies.what: Alice 9-passenger clean-sheet electric commuter (flew once in 2022); claimed $5B order book from Cape Air, DHL and others
companies.signal: Laid off most staff and paused Alice development indefinitely in Feb 2025 while seeking strategic partners

companies.name: Elysian
companies.what: Dutch startup designing the E9X, a 90-seat battery-electric airliner premised on ~400 Wh/kg cells and ~400nm range
companies.signal: Design refined April 2026 (larger wing, more weight); scale model in 2-3 years, full prototype ~2030, service ~2033; Panta Holdings-backed

companies.name: Pipistrel (Textron eAviation)
companies.what: Velis Electro — the world's only EASA type-certified electric airplane, in serial production for flight schools
companies.signal: Hundreds delivered globally; acquired by Textron in 2022 as its eAviation anchor

companies.name: Diamond Aircraft
companies.what: Developing the eDA40 electric trainer with quick-charge capability; parent Wanfeng also absorbed Volocopter's assets
companies.signal: eDA40 in flight test toward certification; established GA manufacturing base

companies.name: Bye Aerospace
companies.what: eFlyer 2/4 electric trainers pursued since the mid-2010s
companies.signal: Certification repeatedly delayed amid persistent funding gaps; program continuation unclear

variations.white_space: The 9-19 seat pure-battery commuter segment has been gutted (Eviation paused, Bye stalled) because ~250-300 Wh/kg pack-level density cannot close the payload-range business case; trainers (Pipistrel) and cargo feeders work today, and the opening reopens only when 400+ Wh/kg cells (solid-state/silicon-anode) reach aviation qualification — battery suppliers, not airframers, hold the bottleneck.

variations.name: Hybrid-electric propulsion & retrofits
variations.description: Pairs combustion engines or turbogenerators with electric motors and batteries to cut fuel burn ~30-50% on regional aircraft, and de-risks certification by retrofitting existing airframes — the pragmatic bridge while batteries and hydrogen mature.

companies.name: Heart Aerospace
companies.what: ES-30 30-seat hybrid-electric regional airliner (battery + turbogenerator 'Independent Hybrid'); built the full-scale Heart X1 demonstrator
companies.signal: ~$145M raised (United, Air Canada, EQT, Breakthrough); relocated HQ from Gothenburg to Los Angeles Apr 2025 and shut Swedish operations; X1 electric first flight planned from Plattsburgh, NY, hybrid X2 to follow

companies.name: Ampaire
companies.what: Hybrid-electric retrofits of in-service aircraft — Eco Caravan (Cessna Grand Caravan with AMP-H570 parallel hybrid) targeting the first FAA STC for hybrid propulsion
companies.signal: Most hybrid flight hours of any startup; STC program in progress with launch operators signed

companies.name: VoltAero
companies.what: Cassio 330 five-seat hybrid aircraft built around Safran's ENGINeUS electric motor plus combustion sustainer; also sells the HPU 210 kit powertrain
companies.signal: Safran ENGINeUS 100 certified Feb 2025 clears its propulsion path; Cassio 330 certification targeted ~2026

companies.name: Electra
companies.what: EL9 'Ultra-STOL' 9-seat hybrid with blown-lift wing — takes off in ~150 ft, opening thousands of unused airstrips with 1,100nm hybrid range
companies.signal: $115M Series B (2025); 2,000+ aircraft in LOIs/pre-orders; FAA Part 23 certification targeted ~2029

companies.name: magniX
companies.what: Supplies certified-track electric propulsion units (magni350/650) powering Harbour Air's eBeaver, Eviation's Alice, and NASA's electrified Dash 7 demo; Samson battery line
companies.signal: NASA electrified powertrain flight demo contract; Clermont Group-owned

companies.name: Safran
companies.what: ENGINeUS 100 became the first type-certified electric aviation motor (EASA, Feb 2025), supplying VoltAero, Diamond eDA40 and others
companies.signal: First-mover certified electric motor among tier-1 engine makers

companies.name: Surf Air Mobility
companies.what: NYSE-listed regional operator developing electrified/hybrid Cessna Caravan powertrains (with magniX) to convert its own and SkyWest-linked fleets
companies.signal: Public (NYSE: SRFM); financially strained but advancing powertrain STC program

variations.white_space: Incumbent engine makers have retreated (Rolls-Royce sold off its electric-propulsion unit; Pratt & Whitney slowed its Dash 8 hybrid demo), and Heart's downsizing shows clean-sheet regional hybrids strain venture funding — certification cost versus a small regional market is the chokepoint, so retrofit STCs on existing airframes (Ampaire-style) are the nearest-term wedge and remain thinly contested.

variations.name: Hydrogen fuel-cell & H2-combustion aircraft plus airport H2 fueling
variations.description: Uses hydrogen in fuel cells driving electric props (or burned directly in turbines) for zero-carbon flight beyond battery range; requires cryogenic or high-pressure storage on board and entirely new airport fueling infrastructure, creating a chicken-and-egg scaling problem.

companies.name: ZeroAvia
companies.what: Hydrogen-electric powertrains (ZA600 for 9-19 seats, ZA2000 for regionals) flight-tested on a Dornier 228; certification path with UK CAA/FAA
companies.signal: Warned Sept 2025 it had cash only to Q1 2026, then closed Series D Dec 2025 (Barclays Climate Ventures, Breakthrough, Horizons, UK National Wealth Fund); ~100-engine order from American Airlines

companies.name: Universal Hydrogen
companies.what: Modular hydrogen capsule logistics ('nespresso pod' fueling) plus Dash 8 fuel-cell conversions; flew a 40-seat testbed in 2023
companies.signal: Shut down June-July 2024 after burning ~$100M (GE, Airbus, American, Toyota-backed); $1B+ conversion backlog evaporated; assets liquidated

companies.name: H2FLY
companies.what: Stuttgart-based fuel-cell aircraft pioneer; flew the world's first piloted liquid-hydrogen fuel-cell flight (HY4, Sept 2023)
companies.signal: Acquired by Joby Aviation in 2021; supplies hydrogen powertrain R&D for Joby's 561-mile hydrogen-electric S4 demo (2024)

companies.name: Beyond Aero
companies.what: French startup designing BYA-1, a clean-sheet hydrogen-electric business jet (~800nm) — the only H2 program native to business aviation
companies.signal: ~$44M+ raised; flew a sub-scale H2 testbed; entry into service targeted ~2030

companies.name: Airbus
companies.what: ZEROe program — the only large-airframer hydrogen airliner effort, now refocused on a fuel-cell concept
companies.signal: Feb 2025: pushed ZEROe from 2035 to the early 2040s and cut budget ~25%; airports scaled back H2 plans in response

companies.name: Fabrum
companies.what: New Zealand maker of liquid-hydrogen storage, liquefaction and airport fueling systems — the ground half of hydrogen aviation
companies.signal: Supplying LH2 ground infrastructure for aviation trials incl. Christchurch/Air New Zealand hydrogen ecosystem work

companies.name: Cranfield Aerospace Solutions
companies.what: Project Fresson — hydrogen fuel-cell retrofit of the 9-seat Britten-Norman Islander for short island routes
companies.signal: Safran-backed; planned merger with Britten-Norman called off in 2024; funding remains tight

companies.name: Stralis Aircraft
companies.what: Australian startup converting a Beech Bonanza then 15-seat B1900D to hydrogen-electric with high-temperature PEM fuel cells
companies.signal: Seed-stage; Brisbane facility; targeting regional Australian routes

variations.white_space: Universal Hydrogen's collapse and the Airbus ZEROe slip to the 2040s froze airline and airport H2 investment — the chicken-and-egg between aircraft and fueling infrastructure is the binding constraint, not the fuel cell; the credible near-term openings are sub-regional retrofits certified under existing rules and airport cryogenic ground equipment (Fabrum is nearly alone), which monetize before any H2 airliner exists.

variations.name: eVTOL & urban air mobility
variations.description: Battery-powered vertical-takeoff air taxis replacing helicopters and congested car trips; zero operational emissions and far quieter, though net climate benefit depends on displacing higher-carbon modes at scale — and the sector just went through a brutal shakeout separating certifiers from the rest.

companies.name: Joby Aviation
companies.what: S4 tilt-prop air taxi; furthest along in FAA certification and first Western commercial launch via Dubai
companies.signal: Flew first FAA-conforming TIA aircraft Mar 2026 (Stage 4); type certificate expected late 2026; acquired Blade's passenger business; Toyota-backed (~$894M)

companies.name: Archer Aviation
companies.what: Midnight 4-passenger eVTOL; UAE early operations and LA28 Olympics partnership; Stellantis manufacturing alliance
companies.signal: Raised ~$850M in 2025; FAA Stage 3; began UAE test flights late 2025; bought Lilium's patent portfolio out of insolvency

companies.name: EHang
companies.what: Autonomous 2-seat EH216-S — the first eVTOL in the world to hold full type, production, and operating certificates (China)
companies.signal: Paid autonomous sightseeing operations running in Chinese cities; one of only two companies globally with the full certificate set as of April 2026

companies.name: Vertical Aerospace
companies.what: UK developer of the VX4 piloted eVTOL; also unveiled a longer-range hybrid-electric variant in 2025
companies.signal: NYSE-listed; survived 2024-25 refinancing led by Mudrick Capital; VX4 in expanding piloted flight test

companies.name: Wisk Aero
companies.what: Autonomous-first 4-seat Gen 6 air taxi — the only major program skipping piloted operations entirely
companies.signal: Wholly owned by Boeing since 2023; targeting commercial launch toward the end of the decade

companies.name: Eve Air Mobility
companies.what: Embraer-backed eVTOL leveraging the parent's certification and manufacturing experience, with one of the largest LOI order books
companies.signal: Raised $150M Jan 2026; prototype in flight test; NYSE-listed

companies.name: AutoFlight
companies.what: Chinese maker of the CarryAll cargo eVTOL — holds Chinese type and production certificates for cargo operations
companies.signal: One of only two companies worldwide with the full certificate set (cargo); backed by Team Global

companies.name: Lilium
companies.what: German 6-seat ducted-fan Lilium Jet promising regional eVTOL range
companies.signal: Insolvent Oct 2024 after Bundestag blocked a €50M guarantee; rescue collapsed; second insolvency Feb 2025, ~1,000 laid off, aircraft scrapped, patents sold to Archer

companies.name: Volocopter
companies.what: German multirotor VoloCity pioneer; post-insolvency pivoted to the VoloXPro, a €490k eVTOL for the general-aviation market
companies.signal: Insolvency Dec 2024; assets bought ~$11M in Mar 2025 by Wanfeng (Diamond Aircraft's Chinese parent); VoloXPro launched Apr 2026 targeting year-end approval

companies.name: Supernal (Hyundai)
companies.what: Hyundai's advanced air mobility unit developing the S-A2 eVTOL with automotive-scale manufacturing ambitions
companies.signal: Paused aircraft development Aug-Sept 2025 after CEO/CTO departures and layoffs; 2026 KAI memorandum aims to restart the program

variations.name: Flight-ops efficiency & contrail avoidance
variations.description: Software that optimizes routes, climb profiles, taxiing and fuel decisions — and now reroutes flights around ice-supersaturated air to avoid warming contrails — cutting 1-5% of fuel burn and potentially a large share of aviation's non-CO2 forcing at near-zero hardware cost.

companies.name: OpenAirlines
companies.what: SkyBreathe — the most widely used airline fuel-efficiency analytics platform, mining flight-data-recorder data for savings and coaching pilots
companies.signal: 80+ airline customers; claims up to 5% fuel reduction with no aircraft modification

companies.name: SATAVIA
companies.what: DECISIONX:NETZERO contrail forecasting and flight-plan optimization, converting avoided warming into tradable climate units; worked with Etihad, KLM and 12 operators
companies.signal: Acquired by GE Aerospace (Aerospace Carbon Solutions unit) Sept 2024 — first contrail-startup exit

companies.name: Google Research / Breakthrough Energy
companies.what: AI contrail-risk maps from satellite + weather data, proven in the largest operational avoidance trial to date
companies.signal: 2025 American Airlines trial across 2,400+ transatlantic flights cut observable contrails ~62% with no statistically significant fuel penalty

companies.name: Flightkeys
companies.what: Vienna-based 5D flight-planning system embedding contrail forecasts and cost-optimal trajectories directly into dispatch
companies.signal: Integrated Google/Breakthrough contrail data for the American Airlines trial; growing share of tier-1 airline flight planning

companies.name: Estuaire
companies.what: French analytics startup quantifying and monitoring airline non-CO2 emissions and route-level climate impact
companies.signal: Engaged by Vueling and Wizz Air (2025) for contrail data analysis and disclosure

companies.name: SITA
companies.what: OptiFlight (acquired from Safety Line) — machine-learning climb-profile and in-flight fuel optimization sold through its huge airline IT footprint
companies.signal: Deployed across dozens of carriers as part of SITA's digital day-of-operations suite

companies.name: Airspace Intelligence
companies.what: Flyways AI — dynamic ATC-aware route re-optimization first deployed fleet-wide with Alaska Airlines
companies.signal: Multi-year Alaska Airlines deployment; venture-backed Series B

variations.white_space: Fuel-efficiency software is crowded, but contrail avoidance — arguably the cheapest large climate lever in all of aviation — has almost no independent commercial players left after SATAVIA sold to GE: there is still no regulatory or market mechanism that pays airlines for avoided contrails (EU non-CO2 MRV only began 2025), so whoever builds the verification-and-credit layer when regulation lands inherits the category.

variations.name: Ultra-efficient airframes & next-gen engines (BWB, open fan, laminar flow)
variations.description: Redesigns the aircraft itself — blended-wing bodies, open-fan engines, truss-braced and laminar-flow wings — to cut fuel burn 20-50% regardless of what fuel is burned; the single biggest efficiency lever for the 2030s fleet and a multiplier on every SAF gallon.

companies.name: JetZero
companies.what: Z4 blended-wing-body 200-250 seat airliner claiming ~50% lower fuel burn; using a US Air Force demonstrator to leapfrog the duopoly
companies.signal: $235M USAF contract (2023); $175M Series B (Jan 2026, B Capital) with United/Alaska equity and conditional orders; $4.7B Greensboro, NC factory announced; demonstrator flight planned 2027

companies.name: CFM International (GE Aerospace + Safran)
companies.what: RISE open-fan engine demonstrator targeting ~20% lower fuel burn and full SAF/H2 compatibility for the next narrowbody generation
companies.signal: Airbus plans RISE-derived open-fan flight tests for its next-generation single-aisle; ground tests progressing

companies.name: Airbus
companies.what: Next-gen single-aisle program (~2035+) wrapping open-fan propulsion, long folding wings, and new materials; keeps BWB on the shelf for larger jets
companies.signal: CEO confirms open-fan baseline studies; 'Wing of Tomorrow' composites program complete

companies.name: Boeing
companies.what: X-66 truss-braced-wing NASA demonstrator exploring ~30% fuel-burn reduction for narrowbodies
companies.signal: Paused the X-66 build in 2025 to refocus on thin-wing research amid company-wide strain — evidence of incumbent slow-walking

companies.name: Otto Aviation
companies.what: Phantom 3500 business jet using super-laminar-flow fuselage to claim ~50-60% lower fuel burn per trip
companies.signal: First flight targeted ~2027; announced Jacksonville, FL production site (2025)

companies.name: Natilus
companies.what: Blended-wing-body freighters (Kona) and a 200-seat passenger BWB concept (Horizon) pitched at 30%+ efficiency gains
companies.signal: Claims multi-billion-dollar pre-order book for cargo BWB; sub-scale prototypes flown

variations.white_space: The Boeing-Airbus duopoly has no clean-sheet aircraft before ~2035 and Boeing even paused its own X-66 efficiency demonstrator, leaving a rare structural opening that JetZero is testing via military-funded demonstrators — but the $10B+ certification-and-industrialization moat means the realistic startup path is defense/cargo first, and almost no one else is attempting it.

variations.name: Low-emission airships & hybrid lighter-than-air cargo
variations.description: Helium-buoyed hybrid and rigid airships trade speed for ~75-90% lower fuel burn (with electric or hydrogen variants planned), targeting remote-area cargo, surveillance, and short-haul passenger niches that need no runways or road infrastructure.

companies.name: Hybrid Air Vehicles
companies.what: Airlander 10 hybrid airship (10-tonne payload) with hydrogen-electric zero-emission variant planned with ZeroAvia
companies.signal: Doncaster UK factory planned for 24 aircraft/yr; ~35 reservations incl. Air Nostrum (20) and a first military order; service entry ~2029

companies.name: LTA Research

variations.white_space: A century of failed revivals (CargoLifter, Lockheed's exited LMH-1) plus helium cost, weather sensitivity, and unsolved variable-buoyancy ground handling keep credible players to three; the opening is narrow but real in remote logistics where the alternative is building roads or flying helicopters — and certification authorities have no modern airship rulebook, so the first type certificate effectively defines the category.
